title: Software Design Philosophies
topic: The design philosophies behind great software products — the mental models, primitives, and principles that made Git, Kafka, DuckDB, SQLite, and Unix category-defining, and how to apply them to invent the next great product

concepts.title: Beyond Features
concepts.brief: Introduction. What makes software products like Git, Kafka, DuckDB, and SQLite successful? From solving problems to changing how we think about them. Design philosophy as a foundation for product innovation.

concepts.title: The Power of a Better Mental Model
concepts.brief: How abstractions reshape problems. From implementation details to conceptual simplicity. Case studies: Git, Kafka, DuckDB.

concepts.title: The Art of the Right Primitive
concepts.brief: Finding the fundamental objects and operations. How good primitives eliminate unnecessary complexity. Case studies: Git commits, Kafka logs, SQL queries.

concepts.title: Simplicity and Composition
concepts.brief: Unix philosophy: small tools, clear interfaces. Minimalism, composability, and deliberate omission. When simplicity becomes a limitation.

concepts.title: Embedded First, Distributed When Necessary
concepts.brief: Eliminating infrastructure and operational overhead. Local-first design and progressive scaling. Case studies: DuckDB and SQLite.

concepts.title: Time, State, and Determinism
concepts.brief: State versus history. Logs, immutability, replay, and reproducibility. Case studies: Kafka, Git, and transactional systems.

concepts.title: Correctness, Extensibility, and Open Interfaces
concepts.brief: Designing around invariants and guarantees. Stable cores and open protocols. Balancing generality, specialization, and control.

concepts.title: Finding the Hidden Problem
concepts.brief: Identifying recurring complexity and unnecessary workflows. Challenging assumptions behind existing solutions. Finding opportunities for new abstractions.

concepts.title: From Philosophy to Product
concepts.brief: Discovering and validating the right primitive. Designing the smallest useful engine. Evaluating adoption, trade-offs, and commercial potential.

concepts.title: A Philosophy of Software Invention
concepts.brief: Conclusion. Principles are tools for reasoning, not universal rules. Great products simplify entire categories of problems. Developing a repeatable approach to software innovation.

summary: Why Git, Kafka, DuckDB, SQLite, and Unix won: the mental models, primitives, and design philosophies underneath them, and a repeatable method for inventing the next category-defining product.
